children: highlighted the company's new 10-year partnership with French football superstar Kylian Mbappé during an investor day event this week. Financial terms were not disclosed, but On
said the arrangement includes both cash and equity, giving Mbappé a stake in the company’s success rather than making him only a paid endorser.
The agreement makes Mbappé a global ambassador and a hands-on product-development partner as Switzerland-based On

enters a new sports vertical. He is expected to work with the company’s teams on high-performance boots and apparel, contributing professional-player feedback and helping shape the brand’s football identity. On plans to introduce football footwear in 2027, drawing on technologies such as LightSpray and CloudTec.
investors, signing one of football’s most recognizable players is a strategic attempt to gain relevance in a category dominated by Nike
. Notably, the company has also brought in Thierry Henry as director of football.
Mbappé described the partnership as the chance to build something new and influence the future of the game. The deal therefore resembles tennis legend Roger Federer’s On

Chief Product Officer Gerald Marolf highlighted that the company has seen from the very first days that its customers are connected to the new signing. "They're already asking what people like Kylian Mbappé is wearing when he turns up with a training ground is decked out in you guess On apparel and On footwear, not just from the football space, but from the lifestyle space. So this just shows how that engine is going to really be a superpower for the other spaces that we have," he stated.
On Wall Street, BTIG views the Mbappé announcement as a significant positive development for On

because it significantly increases the total addressable market by offering exposure to the world's largest sport. Analyst Janine Stichter noted the company acknowledged that their lack of participation in the sport likely led to mindshare loss in the period surrounding the World Cup. "Various estimates place the total size of the global football footwear market around $20B in 2025 and is expected to grow at a ~MSD% CAGR through 2030. We note that the last time Nike disclosed football in its 10K, it was ~$1.7B in wholesale equivalent revenue in F'21 (and has been in excess of $2B previously), with the company recently noting strong DD% growth in the category. On a reported revenue basis, we estimate this puts their category in the $2.5B range, suggesting sizable opportunity if On can successfully scale football," wrote Stitchter.
